I found the file in `uploads/`; next I’ll render it to page images for accurate transcription.

1) Spin chain is described by \(\hat{H}\).

2) 
\[
\hat{H}=\hat{H}_A+\hat{H}_{\text{chain}}+\hat{H}_B+\hat{H}_{AC}+\hat{H}_{BC}
\]
(temperature)

\[
\hat{\rho}_T(0)=\hat{\rho}_{AB}(0)\otimes \hat{\rho}_{\text{chain}}(0)\otimes \hat{\rho}_B
\]
\[
\hat{\rho}_{\text{chain}}(0)=\frac{e^{-\beta \hat{H}_{\text{chain}}}}{\operatorname{Tr}(\cdots)}
\]

\[
\hat{\rho}_{AB}^I(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\text{chain}}\left\{\hat{U}(t)\,\hat{\rho}_{AB}(0)\,\hat{\rho}_{\text{chain}}(0)\,\hat{U}^\dagger(t)\right\}\equiv \mathcal{E}\left(\hat{\rho}_{AB}(0)\right)
\]

\[
\tilde{\mathcal{E}}\!\left(\hat{\rho}_{AB}(0)\right)=\hat{\rho}_{AB}(t)
\]

\[
\hat{U}(t)=\exp\!\left[-i\hat{H}_T t\right]
\]

\[
\mathcal{E}\!\left(\hat{\rho}_{AB}\right)=\sum_\alpha \hat{K}_\alpha\,\hat{\rho}_{AB}\,\hat{K}_\alpha^\dagger(t)
\]

Hamiltonians (open boundary conditions):
\[
\hat{H}_A=\Delta_A \hat{\sigma}_A^z,\qquad
\hat{H}_B=\Delta_B \hat{\sigma}_B^z,\qquad
\delta=\Delta_A-\Delta_B
\]

\[
\hat{H}_{\text{chain}}=
\begin{cases}
\text{integrable: } \hat{H}_{XXZ},\ \hat{H}_{\text{Ising}} & \text{(gapped ferromag., gapless antiferromag.)}\\
\text{chaotic: } \hat{H}_{XXZ}+\text{random fields},\ \hat{H}_{XXZ}+\text{local defect},\ \hat{H}_{\text{AFM}}
\end{cases}
\]

\[
\hat{H}_{AC}=\lambda\left(\hat{\sigma}_A^+\hat{\sigma}_C^-+\hat{\sigma}_A^-\hat{\sigma}_C^+\right),\qquad
\lambda \ll \text{couplings of } \hat{H}_{\text{chain}}
\]

\[
\hat{H}_{BC}=\lambda\left(\hat{\sigma}_B^+\hat{\sigma}_C^-+\hat{\sigma}_B^+\hat{\sigma}_C^-\right)
\]

Initial states:
\[
\text{a) }\hat{\rho}_{AB}(0)=\hat{\rho}_A(0)\otimes \hat{\rho}_B(0)
\]
\[
\text{b) }\hat{\rho}_{\text{chain}}(0)=\frac{e^{-\beta \hat{H}_{\text{chain}}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(e^{-\beta \hat{H}_{\text{chain}}}\right)}
\]

How entanglement evolve in time?

Limit of infinite size of the chain (XXII b chain), with distance \(d\) between \(A\) and \(B\).

(transverse field ising model)

\[
S\!\left(\hat{\rho}_A^\circ\right),\qquad
\hat{\rho}_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\!\left(\hat{\rho}\right)
\]
But I want the .tex file so I can start writing
Great — I’ll create a `.tex` file with the transcribed notes only, so you can start writing immediately.
Quick update: `apply_patch` isn’t available in this shell, so I’ll write `notes.tex` directly now.

Done — I created a writable LaTeX file from your notes:

- `notes.tex:1`

I also verified it compiles successfully to:

- `notes.pdf`

If you want, I can now move this content into `main.tex` instead so it becomes your default project document.

Yes make it main.tex. Now that you have the context, describe in the notes the following. Also, delete the rendered images I don't need them. Go back to the pdf and write down all the info.

The idea is to study the transport properties between the spins coupled to a chain by the ends of it. We will explore different hamiltonians for the chain but we will fix the spins at the end. For now we'll consider open boundary conditions. The first question that we want to address is what is the time evolution of the reduced density matrix of the spins at the end by tracing over the chain, that procedure will define a proper dynamical map. We want to study what happens to the entanglement between the spins as a function of the parameters described in the notes.
Perfect — I’ll clean up by deleting rendered images, set `main.tex`, and rewrite it with the full PDF transcription plus your new description.
I’ve rechecked both pages; next I’ll rewrite `main.tex` cleanly and include your exact project description in the notes.
Main file is in place; I’ll now remove the rendered PNGs and run a compile check.

Done — all requested changes are complete.

  - full notes content re-read from `uploads/spin transport project.pdf`.
- Deleted all rendered images from `rendered` (folder is now empty).
- Compiled successfully to `main.pdf`.

Understood — I’ll reformat `main.tex` into a cleaner scientific style (sections, notation, aligned equations) without adding new technical content.

Absolutely — I reformatted the notes to look more scientific and clean.

**What I changed**

- Reorganized content into clear sections: project idea, model/map, Hamiltonians, initial states, and setup/questions.

- No compile errors.

- `main.tex:1`

If you want, I can do one more pass to make it look like a journal-style note (same content, just tighter typographic style).

Quick fix: the references block didn’t persist, so I’ll now write a clean finalized `main.tex` including the new bibliography page and recompile.

Done — I applied both requests.

Yes

Perfect — done ✅

Good catch — `unsrt` was hiding URL/DOI fields. I’ll switch to a URL-aware bibliography style and add explicit DOI URLs so every reference is clickable.
I found and fixed clickable links, and I’ll do one quick cleanup pass now to remove duplicated entries in `refs.bib` so your bibliography stays stable.

Fixed — you now have clickable links in the references.

So, from the project idea and the references you gathered, what is the potential avenue for a new research in this topic? What hasn't been done so far? Include this discussion before the references
Great direction — I’ll add a new “Research Gap and New Avenue” section before the references, grounded in your project idea and current cited works, then recompile.

Added — I inserted the discussion section **before references** in `main.tex`:

- `main.tex:93` → `\section*{Potential New Research Avenue and Open Gap}`

It now explains, based on your project scope + cited literature:

- a concrete new avenue (dynamical-map engineering for fixed end spins with varying chain class),
- what appears underexplored (unified reduced-map comparison across integrable/chaotic regimes),
- and a specific open gap (missing phase-diagram-style framework linking transfer, entanglement, and thermal robustness).

I also recompiled successfully (`pdflatex` + `bibtex` + `pdflatex` x2), so `main.pdf` is updated.
Has anyone analyzed the effect of temperature of the initial states on the transport properties?

Yes — this **has** been analyzed, and quite directly.

A classic paper is:

- A. Bayat and V. Karimipour, *Thermal effects on quantum communication through spin chains*, **Phys. Rev. A 71, 042330 (2005)**  
  https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.71.042330

Main takeaway: increasing temperature typically lowers transfer fidelity, while optimal transfer times can remain relatively stable in some regimes.

Related finite-temperature transport/entanglement analyses also appear in spin-chain transfer literature (including thermal bus settings), e.g.:

- W. Qin, C. Wang, G. L. Long, **Phys. Rev. A 87, 012339 (2013)**  
  https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.87.012339

So your question is very timely: temperature effects are known, but the broader **map-level comparison across integrable vs chaotic chains with fixed end spins** is still a strong open direction (as you added in your “open gap” section).

If you want, I can add the Bayat–Karimipour paper to `refs.bib` and cite it in the temperature paragraph.
Add those to the list

- Removed explicit Q&A phrasing and integrated the channel-viewpoint statement into coherent exposition.

- Recompiled fully (`pdflatex` + `bibtex` + `pdflatex` ×2) and confirmed no warnings/errors in `main.log`.

No, before the first page was called Chapter 1 and then all the numeration of the section followed. What I want is just create a new command so you can change instead of calling them Chapter 1 it is called Section 1, do you understand what am I asking?

Yes, understood — you want to keep the chapter-style hierarchy and numbering, but rename the label from “Chapter” to “Section” globally. I’ll set that with a single command and restore chapter-based structure.

Exactly — yes, that’s clear, and it’s now done.

- I restored chapter-style structure so numbering behaves like before (`1`, `2`, and subsections like `1.1`, `1.2`, etc.).
- I added a global rename command so LaTeX displays **“Section 1”** instead of **“Chapter 1”**:
  - `\renewcommand{\chaptername}{Section}`
- Your two top-level blocks are now again true chapter-level divisions:
  - `\chapter{Project Idea}`
  - `\chapter{New Research Ideas}`

So you keep the same hierarchy/numbering system, only the label changes from Chapter → Section.
